entry.text: (какое-то интро)
Alright, it's simple. Customer asks for something, you grab it, put it in the bag.
Check the price, set it on the register, push the lever. That's it.
And when they pay, count it right. People get weird about their change.
[Click on an item to read its description. Drag it into the bag to add it to the purchase.]
[To ring up the total, enter the price on the register, then drag the lever down.]
[Count the customer's money, then click on the right banknotes and coins to give them their change.]
[Click on the ? button to talk to the customer and/or ask them to remind or explain their order.]
Let's try it out. Sell me matches and a tin of Morley.

wrong_items.text: That's not what I asked for. Try again.

wrong_price.text: Right stuff, wrong number. Do the math again.

click.text: A tin of Morley tobacco. A box of matches. In the bag, on the register, then the lever.

paying.text: Here's 300. Let's see if you can count.
(Rude. I'll think about giving you your full change.)

wrong_change_under.text: Careful, short-changing is a skill. You clearly don't have it yet.

response.text: Ha. That's the spirit. I like it.
Oopsie doopsie indeed.

wrong_change_under_shortchanging.text: Careful, short-changing is a skill. You clearly don't have it yet.

wrong_change_over.text: You're being generous. That's too much.

checkout.text: See? Easy enough. Now let's try one more time.

checkout_st1.text: Okay, you figured it out, eventually. Let's try again.

entry.text: Round two. Paper for smoke, paper for thought. Two of one, one of the other.

wrong_items_st1.text: That's not what I asked for. Again.

options.text: This place wasn't a tobacconist before

response.text: Yeah, I opened it about a year ago. Year and a half, maybe. Came back to Larris, found the place empty, figured I'd try selling something legal for once.
You know the trope. The big world doesn't want you, so you crawl back to your quirky little hometown to complete your mandatory redemption subplot.
Anyway. Could've ended up somewhere worse than a smoke-stained counter.
Not well. By the time I came back, she had already... found God. Poor guy.
Spent most of her time between the church and the hospital, I guess. Didn't see her here much.
Honestly surprised she didn't sell the place and hand it to the church.
Or maybe you just need her to be the villain. Easier that way.
Praise be to private property.

options.text: What was it you asked for?

response.text: What, riddle too hard? It's just a newspaper and two packs of rolling papers.

wrong_price.text: Want to double-check before I call the math police?

checkout.text: Well done. That's the job - sit here, sell people their little habits, read the paper if you want, and don't let the register jam. If it does, hit it.
...Some people come in more for the conversation than the cigarettes. Whether you listen or not is up to you.

break.text: ...Guess I'll take a look at the news while nobody's here.

entry.text: Morning.
One pack of JCs, the news and a lighter, the kind I won't miss if it goes overboard.

options.text: Back from the big metal boats?

response.text: Yeah. Just stepped off.
Good pay. Bad sleep.
...Not sure it was worth what it did to my head.
Trying not to let it make me all stiff inside. I think it's better to stay gentle.
Gentle? Huh. Like a...
Hey, jellyfish don't sink. They just keep floating. I'll take it.
Yeah. Been through worse, came out smooth. That's the hope.
JC reds. Newspaper. And any cheap, basic lighter.

wrong_items.text: JC reds. Newspaper. And any cheap, basic lighter.

checkout.text: I ate jellyfish as a kid. Thought it was pudding.

checkout_seaglass.text: I tasted sea glass once. Thought it was candy.

after.text: (Well, trawlers were always a thing. But lately, you only see the small boats when they're being sold.)

entry.text: ...And so the daughter returns home. To the dust her mother called holy, and the stillness she mistook for peace.
Step careful - they wait to see what you'll do differently.

response.text: To see what happens, maybe.
Silence is God's first language.

entry.text: Mmm...
The latest paper and Fleuries, please. The mugwort blend, if the Lord still provides.

response.text: Organs are dramatic things. Full of held breath and pressure... too much of it, and even sacred things crack.
Thank God our good old repairman gets along with anything that's fallen out of tune.

options.text: What did your funeral speech mean?

response.text: (какое-то описание че он там буровил я не придумала, просто filler text)
We build meaning like churches - beautiful, hollow, echoing the absence they were built around.
...What's missing is what makes it sacred. That's how eulogies work.
Your mom knew that better than anyone.
Yeah. Got so enlightened her heart checked out.
Well, some prayers answer themselves.

options.text: Which holy blend are we burning today?

response.text: Mugwort Fleuries. And the news. Let it be so.

organ.text: The organ is already in his care.

options.text: Sounds like it had a breakdown

response.text: Like we all do. Nothing unholy about that.
Who else but Yves? Luckily still with help from Pierrick, hanging on beside him...
(I've probably heard of them before. Or maybe just feels like I have. This town's too small.)

options.text: Any plans for a temporary fix?

toFix.text: You think it can't just be quiet for a while? Yesterday there were no chords, and yet... people still prayed.

options.text: A bit of soundtrack never hurts

response.text: That's true. Heaven never minded a little background music.
Exactly. We pray hardest through broken things.

wrong_items.text: We all reach for the wrong thing sometimes.

checkout.text: Funny thing - I'd usually ask someone else to pick these up for me. Then he quit smoking, and I lost my excuse to avoid the walk.
But today it brought me to you, so I'm calling it a good walk.
No more words from me. Be strong and of good courage.

entry.text: Alright, Babette. What are we in the mood for today?
Mm... the pretty Fleuries with the rose petals?
Tempting. But we just spent two hours scraping wax off pews. I think we deserve a little sin.
You're thinking what I'm thinking, aren't you?
One cigar, please. We've earned it.

click.text: ...they've got it all draped up like a dead body.
Don't say that, Lucie. I'll be very sad if our dear organ's really gone for good.
I saw the music fellas in there earlier. They'd already pulled out some pipes.
Oh, so they already let Noose Boy out?
I'm just saying. He's sweet, but he looks like he'd pass out halfway through a rosary.

response.text: Just one cigar, dear.
We only smoke together. That makes it a ritual, not a habit.

wrong_price.text: Hmm. That's not what it cost last time.

checkout.text: Thank you, dear. We'll take this, say our evening prayer and sit under the sky a bit. Let the day settle. And hopefully no one smells temptation and gets nervous...

chckt.text: Yeah. I'd rather not fall apart mid-prayer like that poor organ.

response.text: Oh... Forget it, dear. Just a bad joke.
(Of course. Gossip first, guilt later.)
Hmm. Patience. And patients.
And maybe a bit of forgiveness. Just in case.
Blessings, dear.

entry.text: Interesting. You're definitely not Félix, unless he got prettier.
He died, lucky bastard? Probably no, just playing hide and seek again.
Anyway, my name is Yves. I fix things. Instruments, mostly.
And you are?..

response.text: Oof, my wife says never trust someone whose name has funny letters in it. But maybe I should give you a chance.
Nice to meet you, Just Gail.
Sweet. I can already hear Félix cackling.

entry.text: Well, normally I'd be here for pipe tobacco. But I quit.
So nothing for me today... or maybe the news? No. No, I don't want to know what's going on.
Hmm.
I'll take those tiny papers you roll cigarettes with. And a box of matches. Just in case.

options.text: People are already talking about the organ

response.text: Of course they are. It would've been too boring to just say it was its time. They've got their little theories.
Still. It'll play again. Can't promise a third-day rise, but I've fixed worse.
Oof, I've had enough of the work talk for today, {{name_yves}}, and it's only Monday. Mind if we change the subject?
Nope. I quit last month.
Guy from the brass quartet said smoke messes with your diaphragm. Makes it harder to hold a note.
Can't have that. I've got solos to play.
Tiny cigarette papers and matches.

options.text: You were a smoker for how long?

response.text: Long enough to forget when I started.
I let a nun stick needles in my ears twice a week. Helps with urges.
Hmm, let's see...
Cornet when I'm feeling gentle. Trombone when I'm not. Clarinet... maybe when I don't quite feel like being myself.
Suppose if it takes lungs to play, chances are I've tried it.

wrong_items.text: Creative interpretation, {{name_yves}}, but I asked for something else.

wrong_price.text: Off by a few notes. You might want to tune that register.

wrong_price_yves_abigail.text: So my wife was right about you people with funny letters?

checkout.text: Didn't you say you quit? What's with the papers?
Oh, I just like having them on hand. I've noticed they're the kind of thing people run out of right when they actually need it.
Anyway, thanks for the company and enjoy the rest of the evening. I like it when the town goes quiet. Makes me want to play flugelhorn and think about my funeral arrangements. What about you?

options.text: I'll smoke and pick at my nails
I'll go to sit by the sea

checkout.text: Good plan. Catch you next time, {{name_yves}}.

entry.text: ...You're not Félix.
Nevermind. Hi. Menthol Morleys, please.

response.text: (Not deaf. Just petty.)
Menthol Morleys. I did say it. Clearly.

wrong_items.text: I asked for Menthol Morleys. Not... whatever that is.

entry.text: Surprise. I exist again.
Jesus. I thought you'd be back in an hour. Maybe two. I worked your whole damn shift.
See? Knew you were born for this. Natural cashier.
Anyway. That's enough heroics for today. Here's your cut for the shift. Key's under the counter. Let's close up.

dialog.text: When I was little, the fishmonger was downstairs. The whole building smelled like salt and guts, but after a while, I stopped noticing. Mom never did.
Then it became a photo studio. No more fish, just chemicals, paper and whatever cologne that prickish photographer marinated in daily.
Then I was gone for a while. Now it's a tobacco shop. Out of everything, this smell makes the most sense.
Also... apparently I'm working here now. Somehow got tricked into covering the counter for a bit and then just... stayed.

start.text: ...Bet you want to try one more shift.

response.text: Perfect, I'll need your help on Friday. Key's yours.
Sure. But I'm still counting on you Friday. Key's yours.

start.text: ...Only if you get me a typewriter.
Ha. Planning to crack those newspaper puzzles?
